youtube_video.description:
Read the full guide: https://zudoworks.com/insights/zoho-consultant-australia-nz-local-or-remote/

Looking for a Zoho consultant in Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane or Auckland? Zoho work happens inside your own Zoho account, on Zoho's servers, through a browser, so a consultant in the next suburb and a team in another country log in to the same screens. Distance still changes a few things: who can sit in your office, which hours you can reach them, how GST is handled and what privacy law asks of you. The guide was checked against the pages of Zoho, the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner, the New Zealand Privacy Commissioner, the ATO and Inland Revenue on 25 November 2026. It is general information, not legal or tax advice.

Chapters
00:00 Local or remote: the postcode matters less
00:06 Same account, same screens
00:12 When to choose a local firm
00:17 When a remote team works as well
00:22 Create the account yourself: zoho.com.au
00:29 Who logs in, from where (APP 8)
00:37 Hours in your time zone, and GST
00:42 Read the six checks

Key points from the guide
- Choose a local firm for on-site workshops, accounting-led projects, hands-on training or a contract under Australian or New Zealand law.
- A remote team suits defined builds: Zoho Creator apps, Deluge scripts, integrations, CRM set-up and fixes. Many businesses mix the two, with one written scope between them.
- Zoho assigns a data centre from your location when the account is created. Accounts in Zoho's Australian data centre sign in at accounts.zoho.com.au, and moving later is not self-service.
- Australia: the OAIC says giving personal information to an overseas contractor is in most circumstances a disclosure under APP 8, and you remain accountable.
- New Zealand: under section 11 of the Privacy Act 2020, a provider holding information solely on your behalf is not treated as holding it. Your organisation stays responsible.
- GST: the reverse charge on an overseas invoice applies only in some cases in Australia, and in New Zealand below 95 per cent taxable use. Ask your accountant.
- Ask every firm, local or remote, for its working hours written in your own time zone, for summer and winter, and where everyone who will log in is based.

The full guide also has a side-by-side table and a 12-question checklist for before you sign.

Choosing a Zoho consultant or developer in Australia or New Zealand? Read the guide and get in touch through zudoworks.com.

Should an Australian or New Zealand business only hire a Zoho consultant in its own city?

Not necessarily. Zoho work is done inside your own Zoho account, on Zoho's servers, through a browser. A consultant in the next suburb and a team overseas log in to the same screens.

Distance still changes four things, and our new guide works through each one:

1. Who can be in the room. Process workshops, accounting-led projects and hands-on training are where a local firm earns its place.
2. Where the data sits. Zoho sets the data centre when the account is created. Create it yourself, in your name, and check the sign-in ends in zoho.com.au.
3. Who has access. In Australia, the OAIC says overseas access to personal information is in most cases a disclosure under APP 8. In New Zealand, section 11 treats a provider acting only for you differently. The rules follow the people, so ask every firm where its team is based.
4. Hours and GST. Get working hours written in your own time zone for summer and winter, and ask your accountant how GST applies to an overseas invoice.

A question I hear from Australian and New Zealand business owners: "Do we need a Zoho consultant in our city?"

My honest answer is: it depends on the work, not the postcode.

Zoho work happens inside your own account, online. Whoever you hire logs in to the same screens.

So I ask people to split the project in two.

The first half is deciding how work should flow. If sales, operations and accounts still disagree, a day in one room with a whiteboard settles more than a week of video calls. That is where a local firm is worth it.

The second half is building: Creator apps, Deluge scripts, integrations, CRM set-up. That can be specified in writing and shown in weekly demos. A remote team can do that well.

Whoever you choose, a few checks matter more than the location:

→ Create the Zoho account yourself, in your name, and check the sign-in ends in zoho.com.au
→ Ask where everyone who will log in is based, including subcontractors
→ In Australia, overseas access to personal information is usually a disclosure under APP 8, so agree the contract terms first
→ Get the firm's hours written in your own time zone, summer and winter
→ Ask your accountant how GST applies to an overseas invoice

Full disclosure: we are a remote team ourselves, so weigh my view with that in mind. The guide says plainly where a local firm is the better choice.

The cheapest mistake to avoid when you hire a Zoho firm: letting them create your Zoho account.

Zoho assigns a data centre from the location of whoever signs up. If someone overseas creates it for you, your data may end up in another region, and moving it later is not self-service.

That is the first of six checks I would make before signing with any Zoho consultant in Australia or New Zealand, local or remote:

1. The account is created by you, in your name, with your own super admin.
2. The sign-in address ends in zoho.com.au.
3. Working hours are written in your time zone, for summer and winter. Queensland, WA and the NT do not change their clocks, and many supplier countries do not either.
4. You know where everyone who will log in is based, including any subcontractors.
5. Your accountant has confirmed how GST applies to the invoice.
6. You have seen similar work on a screen share, and started with a small paid task.

None of these depends on whether the firm is down the road or across the world. They are the same questions for everyone, and a good firm will answer them without hesitation.

I built the six checks, and the rules behind them, into four slides.

We are a remote team, so I have an interest here. Where a local firm is the better choice, the guide says so.
